evals.name: restructure-bookings-route
evals.prompt: este route handler de reservas de clases ya tiene 100 lineas y cada vez que tocamos algo se rompe otra cosa. Ademas no lo puedo testear sin levantar la base y stripe. Como lo reorganizo? te paso el archivo (app/api/bookings/route.ts)
evals.expected_output: Diagnosis first, then business rules (capacity, weekly limit, pricing) extracted into pure testable functions, a use-case layer, a thin handler, input validation at the boundary, and ordered migration steps.
assertions: A diagnosis of the current problems precedes the proposed structure
Capacity, weekly-limit and pricing rules become functions that take data as arguments with no db or stripe calls inside
The route handler is reduced to parse input, call a use case, shape the response
The request body is validated with a schema at the boundary
Dependencies (db, stripe, email, clock) are passed in rather than imported inside the use case
Migration steps are ordered and each keeps the app shippable
The current time is not read via new Date() inside the extracted rules

evals.name: scaffold-gym-app-structure
evals.prompt: arranco de cero una app para administrar el gimnasio: socios, cuotas, reservas de clases y control de acceso. Next.js 15 con app router, typescript y postgres. Como organizo las carpetas para que no se me haga un quilombo en 6 meses? somos 2 devs
evals.expected_output: Feature-first structure with a shared layer, explicit dependency direction, per-feature public index.ts, boundary validation, and an explicit warning against over-abstracting for a 2-dev project.
assertions: Proposes feature-first folders rather than top-level components/hooks/services buckets
Each feature exposes a public index.ts contract
Warns against over-abstraction given a 2-dev team
Addresses the client/server boundary for the Next.js app router
Names a mechanical way to enforce module boundaries (lint rule or equivalent)
